The active time-elements rule says to add `<time>` for a date with month and day but no year, as `datetime="MM-DD"`. It wraps only the date phrase, here "5 November", and leaves the weekday-less "morning" and the punctuation outside. The surrounding bare `<i>` dateline is kept, as em-vs-i step 4 allows. SE's lack of `<time>` is not an error.

se-llm step: [Semantic] Apply letter-subroles (44 changes)
SE correct leftover presentational class
The `class="r"` is a carried-over Gutenberg alignment hook. The supplied manual gives no CSS for it, and the signature semantic already carries the meaning, with right alignment coming from the footer pattern. SE's bare `epub:type="z3998:signature"` is cleaner; if se-llm's stylesheet defines `.r`, the class would be harmless, but nothing supplied shows that.

Lint resolution

Result: failed. Owner and checker model: claude-opus-5-5. Repair rounds: 1. Owner calls: 5; checker calls: 5.

Why it stopped: 2 lint finding(s) unresolved: the reviewer says this needs a repair, which belongs to its owning pass or rule; 3 lint code(s) left by their owners: s-023, s-078, s-081; see …/bram-stoker_dracula.se-llm/lint-defects.md

What the independent checker rejected:

  • In three files, the every-occurrence '<br/></p>' edits reach fewer paragraphs than the finding reports. chapter-7.xhtml reports 4 flagged <p> (lines 17, 20, 35, 44) but has only 3 occurrences of '<br/></p>'. chapter-12.xhtml reports 6 (lines 79, 81, 87, 100, 102, 107) but has only 5. chapter-14.xhtml reports 11 (lines 30, 32, 36, 45, 48, 97, 98, 102, 111, 112, 116) but has only 10. Each paragraph can end in at most one '<br/></p>', so one flagged paragraph in each file must end some other way (for example with whitespace or a line break between <br/> and </p>), and these edits leave its trailing <br/> in place. The rationale's claim that the file-wide replacement covers every flagged paragraph is contradicted by these counts. Each of those three paragraphs needs its own line-targeted edit that removes only its final <br/>.
  • The chapter-24 'Van Helsing' occurrence is properly kept, but the chapter-7 occurrence is not supported. The only evidence that 'The' belongs to the name is that it sits inside the producer's own <i epub:type="se:name.publication.newspaper"> markup, which is the very thing in question. SE practice puts a periodical's leading article in lowercase and outside the italics ('Cutting from the <i …>Dailygraph</i>'). Acceptance here needs the rule or source evidence that makes 'The' part of the title, or else the chapter-7 heading should be fixed to SE's form.
